about: JDE Peet's is an Amsterdam-based global coffee and tea company, created by the 2020 merger of Jacobs Douwe Egberts and Peet's Coffee. Brands include Douwe Egberts, Jacobs, L'OR, Tassimo, Senseo, Peet's and Pickwick, sold in more than 100 markets with revenue of roughly 9 billion euros. Customers are consumers via retailers and foodservice. Controlled by JAB Holding and listed on Euronext Amsterdam from 2020; Keurig Dr Pepper agreed to acquire it in 2025. Well-known grocery brands in Europe.

Sucro Sourcing is a US food ingredient processing company that offers sugar and sweetener sourcing, refining and supply, and in recent years has focused on sugar refining operations in the Southeastern US. The input shows reported funding of about $839 million. Customers are food and beverage manufacturers. B2B ingredients supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Luckin Coffee is a Xiamen, China-based coffee chain, founded in 2017, with more than 24,000 stores in China, selling coffee, tea and snacks mostly through a mobile app for pickup and delivery. It overtook Starbucks in China store count. After a 2020 accounting fraud scandal it was delisted from Nasdaq, restructured and traded over the counter, and is controlled by Centurium Capital. Very high consumer brand awareness in China, with global expansion into Singapore and the US starting.

wiki.title: Luckin Coffee
wiki.text: Luckin Coffee Inc. (Chinese: 瑞幸咖啡; pinyin: Ruìxìng Kāfēi) is a Chinese coffee company and coffeehouse chain founded in Beijing in 2017. In the first half of 2026, Luckin had 35,000 stores globally. The company operates shops, stores, and kiosks that offer coffee, tea, and food, generally at lower prices than their competitors. Purchases can only be made using an online app. Luckin is headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian. The company has expanded rapidly since its founding, and by 2019, its stores outnumbered Starbucks locations in China. about: Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB) is the Indian bottling and distribution arm of the Coca-Cola system, headquartered in Gurugram with a base shown in Bengaluru, producing and selling Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Thums Up, Limca, Maaza and Minute Maid across India through plants and millions of retail outlets. It is owned by The Coca-Cola Company, which agreed in 2025 to sell a stake of about 40 percent to the Jubilant Bhartia group. Mass consumer reach and an active sponsor of cricket and events in India.

Fruitist is a Los Angeles-based food and beverage company that, according to its Crunchbase profile, designs, grows and distributes premium fruit. Customers are likely retailers and consumers buying branded fresh fruit, but products, scale, ownership and funding details are not confirmed from the input. Consumer-facing food brand with unknown awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Starbucks is the world's largest coffee chain, headquartered in Seattle, Washington and listed on Nasdaq (SBUX). It operates about 40,000 company-owned and licensed stores in over 80 countries, selling coffee, tea, food and packaged goods, with about 380,000 employees and revenue near 36 billion dollars. Founded 1971. Customers are mainstream consumers; also earns from Nestle licensing of packaged products. One of the most recognised consumer brands globally with loyalty programme and heavy marketing.

wiki.title: Starbucks
wiki.text: Starbucks Corporation is an American multinational chain of coffeehouses and roastery reserves headquartered in Seattle, Washington. It was founded in 1971 by Jerry Baldwin, Zev Siegl, and Gordon Bowker at Seattle's Pike Place Market initially as a coffee bean wholesaler. Starbucks was converted into a coffee shop serving espresso-based drinks under the ownership of Howard Schultz, who was chief executive officer from 1986 to 2000 and led the aggressive expansion of the franchise across the West Coast of the United States.

about: Cbc, the Guatemala-based Central America Beverage Corporation, is a food and beverage company known as a major bottler for PepsiCo products and local brands across Central America and the Caribbean. The input shows a franchising and beverage focus with funding of $875 million. Strong regional consumer reach. CBC distributes beverages and also operates franchise restaurants and other businesses across Central America and the Caribbean.

about: Italian tomato and prepared foods producer, based in Angri, Campania, supplying canned tomato products, beverages and sauces to retailers across Europe, with a large UK trade. B2B and private label with limited consumer recognition. Sells canned tomatoes, pasta sauces, fruit juices and fruit-based drinks for retailers and private label across Europe. Founded 1954. Low consumer recognition. La Doria is among the leading Italian suppliers of canned tomato products to British supermarkets.

Global tea brand Lipton, whose tea business Unilever spun into Ekaterra (sold to CVC in 2022), selling Yellow Label and other teas; ready-to-drink Lipton Ice Tea is made under licence with PepsiCo. Consumer packaged goods sold in over 100 countries, with the Lipton Ice Tea brand licensed to PepsiCo. Global recognition.

Potbelly Sandwich Works is a US fast-casual sandwich chain headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. It serves toasted sandwiches, salads, soups and milkshakes in roughly 450 shops, mostly company-owned plus franchised stores across the US, with delivery and catering. Founded in 1977, it earns money from food sales and franchise fees. It is listed on Nasdaq (PBPB). Recognisable consumer restaurant brand with regional strength in the Midwest and with moderate national awareness.

wiki.title: Potbelly Sandwich Shop
wiki.text: Potbelly Sandwich Shop, also known as Potbelly Sandwich Works, is an American fast-casual restaurant chain with over 400 locations that focuses on submarine sandwiches and milkshakes. It is owned by RaceTrac.

about: Zabka Group is the operator of Poland's largest convenience store network, Zabka, with more than 10,000 small neighbourhood stores, plus the Freshmarket concept and the Jush! digital services, and a growing presence in Romania. It sells groceries, ready meals and services such as parcel pick-up to consumers, and earns from retail margins and franchise operations. Registered in Luxembourg and majority backed by CVC, it listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in 2025. Very high consumer recognition in Poland.

Haidilao is a Chinese hot pot restaurant chain founded in Sichuan in 1994, known for table-side noodle-pulling, attentive service and free extras. Its holding company in Beijing is listed in Hong Kong (6862). It operates more than 1,300 restaurants in mainland China and abroad in Asia, North America, Europe and Australia, with annual revenue in the tens of billions of yuan. Haidilao is a very high-profile consumer brand in China and well known among Asian diaspora, and it has done sponsorship and partnerships.

Coca-Cola HBC is the second largest bottler of Coca-Cola products by volume, producing and distributing Coca-Cola, Fanta, Sprite, Monster, Costa Coffee and Finlandia in 29 countries across Europe, Eastern Europe and Africa. Revenue near 10 billion euros. Headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, with operational roots in Greece; Coca-Cola Company and Kar-Tess Holding are major shareholders. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (CCH) and Athens. B2B bottler that operates well-known Coca-Cola brands.

wiki.title: Coca-Cola HBC
wiki.text: Coca-Cola HBC AG, formerly known as Coca-Cola Hellenic Bottling Company or just Coca-Cola Hellenic, is the world's third-largest Coca-Cola anchor bottler in terms of volume with sales of more than 2 billion unit cases. Coca-Cola HBC's shares are primarily listed on the London Stock Exchange with a secondary listing on the Athens Stock Exchange. The company is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index. Coca-Cola HBC has been named the industry leader among beverage companies in the 2014 Dow Jones Sustainability Index and is also included in the FTSE4Good Index.

about: Kimberly-Clark is a US consumer products company making Huggies diapers, Kleenex tissues, Cottonelle, Scott, Kotex and Depend, plus Kimberly-Clark Professional products, sold in 175 countries. Revenue near 20 billion dollars. Headquartered in Irving, Texas; founded 1872. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (KMB). In November 2025 it agreed to acquire Kenvue (Tylenol, Neutrogena) in a deal valued at around 48.7 billion dollars. Strongly visible household brands with a history of sports tie-ins.

wiki.title: Kimberly-Clark
wiki.text: Kimberly-Clark Corporation is an American multinational consumer goods and personal care corporation that produces mostly paper-based consumer products. The company manufactures sanitary paper products and surgical & medical instruments. Kimberly-Clark brand name products include Kleenex facial tissue, Kotex feminine hygiene products, Cottonelle, Scott and Andrex toilet paper, Wypall utility wipes, KimWipes scientific cleaning wipes and Huggies disposable diapers and baby wipes. Founded in Neenah, Wisconsin, in 1872 and based in the Las Colinas section of Irving, Texas, since 1985, the company operated its own paper mills around the world for

about: Hanesbrands is a Winston-Salem, North Carolina apparel company making basics under the Hanes, Bonds, Maidenform, Playtex and Bali brands (it sold its Champion activewear brand to Authentic Brands in 2024). It sells innerwear and basics through mass retailers, wholesale and online in the Americas, Australia and Europe, with revenue of roughly $3.5 billion. Listed on NYSE (HBI); Gildan agreed to acquire it in 2025. Household brand with large consumer recognition.

wiki.title: Hanesbrands
wiki.text: Hanesbrands Inc. is an American multinational clothing company based in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Employing 65,300 people internationally, it owns several clothing brands, including Hanes, Playtex, Bali, L'eggs, Just My Size, Barely There, Wonderbra, Maidenform, Berlei, and Bonds. The company was acquired by Gildan in 2025.

about: Merama is a Mexican e-commerce aggregator, founded in 2021, that acquires and scales Amazon and online brands in Latin America, particularly in Mexico, Brazil and Colombia. It provides funding, operational expertise and resources to sellers, and it earns money by owning and selling consumer products across home, beauty and sports categories through online marketplaces. Based in Mexico City, it raised hundreds of millions of dollars in venture and debt financing. Limited direct brand recognition because the brands it owns are marketed separately.

about: FINN is a German car subscription provider where customers get a new or used car with insurance, registration and maintenance included for a monthly fee, fully online, with cars delivered to the door. Headquartered in Munich; founded 2019. Raised funding from investors such as BMW iVentures, with an operational scale in the tens of thousands of cars. Consumer-facing brand with growing awareness in Germany.

about: Clearco is a Toronto fintech, formerly Clearbanc, that offers revenue-based financing to e-commerce and software companies, advancing cash for marketing and inventory in exchange for a share of future revenue. It restructured in 2022-23, cutting staff and exiting several markets. Funding of about $960m includes equity and debt. Private. B2B fintech known to online merchants, with no consumer brand awareness.

Settle is a US B2B cash-flow management and financial technology platform serving e-commerce and consumer brands, helping them manage payables, pay suppliers and access working capital. The input lists reported funding of about $761 million, most likely credit facilities. B2B fintech with limited public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Autodoc is a Berlin-based online retailer of vehicle spare parts and accessories, founded in 2008 by Alexej Erdle, selling over a million parts to drivers and garages in more than 25 European countries via its own web shops. Revenue is over a billion euros. Reported funding of about 580 million euros; an IPO was planned but postponed in 2023. Consumer e-commerce brand with high awareness in Germany and Eastern Europe, with football and motorsport sponsorship.

wiki.title: Autodoc
wiki.text: AUTODOC SE is an e-commerce company selling auto parts and related products in 27 European countries. Its main customers are individuals and smaller workshops. The company sells via its online shops, mobile app, AUTODOC MARKETPLACE, and third-party marketplaces.

about: TaoCheChe is a Chinese automotive e-commerce company, associated with the Alibaba ecosystem, that sells new cars online and offers car-related services to buyers, working with dealers and manufacturers. It is based in China (Shanghai). The input lists reported funding of about $591 million. Consumer-facing platform with moderate awareness in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: TaoCheChe is an innovative company focused on the field .

about: CARS24 is an Indian used-car platform headquartered in Gurugram, founded in 2015 by Vikram Chopra and others. It lets consumers sell cars through inspection and instant pricing, and buy certified used cars via online listings, with financing and insurance add-ons, and operated in the UAE and Australia before scaling back. Backed by SoftBank, Tiger Global and DST, it reached a valuation of about 3 billion dollars. Strong consumer brand in India, known for cricket sponsorships.

Petco is a US pet specialty retailer selling pet food, supplies and live animals, and providing grooming, training and veterinary services through Vetco clinics, with about 1,500 stores and an online business. Customers are pet owners, with revenue about $6 billion. Headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 1965. Listed on Nasdaq (WOOF) since 2021, after being owned by CVC Capital and CPP Investments. Strong consumer brand across the US, with stadium naming rights at Petco Park.

Suning.com is a Chinese retailer of electronics, appliances and general merchandise, operating thousands of physical stores and an online platform, logistics and financial services. Founded in 1990 and based in Nanjing, with revenue in the hundreds of billions of yuan at its peak. It ran into financial trouble in 2021 and was bailed out by a group of Jiangsu state-linked investors. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002024). Its parent group owned Inter Milan until 2024 and has deep sports sponsorship experience. Strong Chinese consumer brand.

Zoomcar is a Bengaluru-based car-sharing marketplace in India and emerging markets, connecting car owners with renters who drive themselves, with hosts earning rental income. Founded in 2013, it also operates in Egypt, Indonesia and Vietnam, and listed on Nasdaq (ZCAR) in 2023 via a SPAC merger with Innovative International Acquisition Corp. Customers are urban Indian consumers and travellers. Moderate consumer awareness in India, with a small revenue base and losses.

Marelli is an automotive components supplier formed in 2019 by the merger of Magneti Marelli and Calsonic Kansei, headquartered in Saitama, Japan, making lighting, electronics, powertrain, thermal and interior parts for automakers. Owned by KKR. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US in June 2025. Revenue was around 10 billion dollars. B2B, with heritage in motorsport through Magneti Marelli electronics.
